name: Landeck
kurzbeschreibung: Historic town at the confluence of the Inn and Sanna, featuring Schloss Landeck and the Altes Kino.
beschreibung:
Overview

Landeck is the bustling district capital of the Landeck district in the Tyrolean Oberland. Situated at an elevation of 816 metres in a commanding valley basin where the Sanna River flows into the Inn, the town is enclosed by the Lechtal Alps to the north, the Samnaun group to the south, and the Ötztal Alps to the east. With approximately 7,700 residents, Landeck serves as the economic, educational, and cultural epicenter of Western Tyrol. Set strategically near the border triangle of Austria, Switzerland, and Italy, and acting as the gateway to the Arlberg, Paznaun, and Reschen passes, the town unites historic fortress heritage with alpine adventures on Mount Venet.

History

Landeck's key geographical position as an alpine crossroads made it significant as early as Roman times, when the Via Claudia Augusta passed through the basin. Around 1290, Count Meinhard II of Tyrol constructed Castle Landeck atop a sheer rocky promontory overlooking the Inn, serving as a princely administrative court and defensive fortress guarding the approaches to the Arlberg and Reschen passes. For generations, Landeck was tied to the poignant history of the "Schwabenkinder" – impoverished peasant children sent on foot across the passes to work seasonal jobs in southern Germany. Landeck received full town charter status in 1923. The late-Gothic parish church of the Assumption, consecrated in 1493, houses the renowned Schrofenstein winged altarpiece, a masterwork of Tyrolean woodcarving.

Getting There

Landeck serves as the primary transport junction for Western Tyrol with exceptional connectivity. Landeck-Zams railway station, located along the trans-alpine Arlberg line, is served hourly by international Railjet and EuroCity services from Vienna, Zurich, and Bregenz. For motorists, the A12 Inntal Autobahn converges here with the S16 Arlberg Expressway, seamlessly linking with the B180 Reschen federal road towards South Tyrol and Italy. A comprehensive regional bus terminal at the station connects travellers to all adjoining alpine valleys, including Paznaun, Kaunertal, and the Upper Inn Valley.

Tips

A tour of Castle Landeck is unmissable: its district museum showcases poignant exhibitions on regional history, the lives of the Schwabenkinder, and rotating contemporary art galleries. Taking the Venet Cable Car in neighbouring Zams brings visitors swiftly to Mount Krahberg at 2,208 metres, featuring a 360-degree mountain panorama, scenic trails, and family ski slopes. Whitewater enthusiasts flock to the turbulent waves of the Sanna River for world-class kayaking and rafting. Another rewarding natural sight nearby is the Zammer Lochputz gorge, with its mystical waterfall and illuminated canyon walkways.
